inspection_summary: Inspected all 784 normalized lines. The recoverable mathematical core is a computational-certification pipeline plus an exact census of Gram-block and Gram-interval behavior: reruns remove an earlier sign-handling confound, machine-specific arithmetic enters a conservative error analysis, and exceptional local zero patterns expose both the power and the limits of Rosser-rule-based separation. Tables are usable where their governing prose fixes their meaning; graph traces and a few formulas remain text-extraction dependent.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the finite verification claim, simplicity claim, and the statistical and exceptional-zero phenomena reported.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction and computational provenance
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the verified range, continuation condition, machine partition, reruns, and cross-platform checks underlying the certificate.

sections_inspected.label: Computation of Z(t) and error analysis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Describes vectorized evaluation, arithmetic error modeling, dominant approximation errors, conservative bounds, and sign resolution.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Gives exact block-length and block-type counts, observed drift, rare unclassifiable patterns, and their relation to rule exceptions.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares distributions across height, states finite-sample cautions, records rare first occurrences, and supplies a counting consistency check.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Classifies exceptions, explains recovery of missing zero pairs, studies local extrema of S(t), and relates unusual zero geometry to large values of Z(t).

accepted_units.title: Finite zero verification assembled from separated ranges and a boundary overrun
accepted_units.why_material: The claim is not presented as a raw count: distinct machine runs cover adjacent Gram-index ranges, five further blocks beyond the target satisfy Rosser's rule, and an imported theorem converts that coverage into the stated critical-line and simplicity result.
accepted_units.context_note: The span crosses a page footer; Theorem 3.2 is only cited, so the logical conversion cannot be reconstructed from this source alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Gram-index subscripts are OCR-noisy, but the prose, interval endpoints, five-block continuation, and final claim are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Rerun design removes sign-shift contamination and supplies independent agreement checks
accepted_units.why_material: Earlier counts were inexact because uncertain Gram-point signs triggered argument shifts; recomputation evaluates a higher-accuracy method immediately, while two other ranges are rerun and agree exactly. This is reusable computational-audit logic rather than mere provenance.
accepted_units.context_note: The method labels and referenced algorithms are defined in prior papers, but the confound and repair are explicit here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Some interval subscripts are degraded; the affected ranges and exact-agreement claim remain readable.

accepted_units.title: Vectorized Z(t) evaluation preserves a hierarchy of approximation and arithmetic errors
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes speedup in the dominant summation from correctness analysis, extends the analyzed height range, models truncated single/double precision explicitly, and identifies interpolation and Riemann-Siegel truncation as machine-independent dominant terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Detailed derivations are deliberately omitted and cited to earlier work; this unit captures the error-budget architecture, not a self-contained proof of the bounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted summation and powers are formula-risky, while the prose distinction among vectorization, arithmetic precision, and dominant errors is clear.

accepted_units.title: Conservative error bounds turn computed Gram-point values into certified signs
accepted_units.why_material: Analytic error bounds are reduced to fixed, deliberately looser operational thresholds, and the high-accuracy fallback determines every Gram-point sign encountered. This connects numerical approximation to the discrete sign evidence needed by the separation procedure.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact functional form of the displayed bounds is OCR-sensitive, but the safe and implemented bounds and the no-failure observation are explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires scan verification before reusing the exponents or displayed inequality verbatim; qualitative certification logic is text-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Exact Gram-block census reveals slow redistribution toward longer blocks
accepted_units.why_material: Unshifted sign computation makes the counts exact, and equal-sized Gram-index windows show length-one blocks decreasing while lengths at least two increase; the total census anchors later distributional claims.
accepted_units.context_note: Table 1 is dense and OCR spacing is degraded, so individual entries should be machine-checked against the scan before quantitative reuse.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on table layout for exact per-window counts; the average length and directional trends are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Gram-block type symmetry coexists with rare patterns outside the standard classification
accepted_units.why_material: The type census records symmetric-looking mass across positions, isolates rare zero-patterns that do not fit the inherited classification, and observes that the missing pair tends toward outer intervals for certain lengths while refusing to infer a limit law for undersampled long blocks.
accepted_units.context_note: The definition of type (j,k) is imported from a cited paper; this span supports comparative structure and explicit exceptions, not a standalone definition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact table cells require layout-aware verification; the unclassified patterns and finite-sample caveat are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Height comparison and first-occurrence data separate apparent convergence from rarity
accepted_units.why_material: Three separated windows suggest stabilization for block lengths three through six, while sparse longer blocks are explicitly withheld from that conclusion; first-occurrence data show that nonobservation and late appearance are material sampling effects.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit includes Tables 3 and 4 because the surrounding prose relies on both distribution percentages and occurrence indices.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Table values are mostly readable but spacing and some digits are OCR-risky; qualitative comparisons are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Zero-count balance checks interval censuses and exposes systematic occupancy drift
accepted_units.why_material: The source adjusts window boundaries away from bad Gram points and gives a conservation relation between empty and multiply occupied intervals when no missing pair crosses an endpoint. The same exact census shows one-zero intervals declining as zero-, two-, three-, and four-zero intervals rise.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed counting identity at line 346 is corrupted in extraction; its endpoint conditions and combinatorial purpose are stated in prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Do not reuse the OCR form of the identity without scan verification; Table 5 totals and trends also require layout-aware parsing for exact numbers.

accepted_units.title: Post-hoc recovery of missing zero pairs suggests an integrated search and its first failure mode
accepted_units.why_material: Every observed Rosser-rule exception is repaired by finding the missing pair in an adjacent block, motivating integration into the main separation program; the authors then construct the simplest neighboring-block pattern where that local strategy would fail.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposed failure pattern is hypothetical and its first occurrence is unknown, so it is an obstruction to a method, not an observed counterexample.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Zero-pattern strings and the adjacent-block logic are clearly recoverable from text.

accepted_units.title: Rosser-rule exceptions form a sparse, asymmetric taxonomy with still-empty types
accepted_units.why_material: The narrative and Table 6 jointly distinguish length-two and length-three exception patterns, their frequencies, first indices for rare forms, and a defined but unobserved type, preserving absence as finite-range evidence rather than impossibility.
accepted_units.context_note: The table's positional diagram is needed to map every type number to its full neighboring pattern.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Type-frequency totals are readable; exact positional layouts and note indices should be verified against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Exception frequencies and local extrema of S(t) show a slowly thickening tail
accepted_units.why_material: Counts by successive Gram-index windows suggest growth in common exception types, every exception is paired with a local-extreme computation, threshold exceedances are cataloged, and three successive groups suggest a very slow increase in extreme magnitudes.
accepted_units.context_note: The trend is descriptive and nonmonotone; the source neither supplies a limiting distribution nor a causal explanation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Tables 7-9 are layout-sensitive and several symbols are degraded; threshold definitions and qualitative trend are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Rare exception plots and normalized spacing expose local zero geometry beyond block labels
accepted_units.why_material: The selected graphs realize newly observed exception types, and the closest observed pair is compared using mean local spacing, turning an absolute gap into a scale-free local statistic.
accepted_units.context_note: The plots cannot display every zero at printed scale; the authors state that magnification is required, so the captions are evidence summaries rather than direct visual certification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The normalized-spacing formula is readable but typographically degraded; plot-based details require the retained page image.

accepted_units.title: Extreme Gram-point values of Z(t) occur beside atypically wide local zero gaps
accepted_units.why_material: The largest observed positive and negative Gram-point values are linked to explicit neighboring block patterns, and in both cases the adjacent zeros are separated by several local Gram-interval lengths, connecting amplitude extremes to local spacing geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: These are two observed configurations and do not establish a general amplitude-gap law.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One extracted index/value is noisy; block zero-patterns and approximate relative gaps are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Block-type data motivate an unknown length-conditioned convex distribution
accepted_units.why_material: The discussion compresses the tables into a falsifiable modeling target: a discrete convex distribution over block types whose shape depends on block length, while explicitly labeling the governing probabilistic law as unknown.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an empirical conjecture invited by finite-range data, not a proved limiting law.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: No material representation dependency; the claim is prose-explicit.

accepted_units.title: A higher finite verification bound can sharpen conditional consequences without proving RH
accepted_units.why_material: The authors distinguish a larger verified critical-line range from a global proof and point instead to downstream results parameterized by a finite verified height, preserving the proper logical role of computation.
accepted_units.context_note: The consequences are only cited and were not traced in the paper, so no particular improvement is claimed here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted zeta symbol is corrupted at line 717, but the conditional statement and scope limitation are clear.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Layered finite-verification certificate
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Range partition, deliberate overrun beyond the target, corrected sign handling, cross-machine reruns, and conservative evaluation bounds form complementary layers of a finite zero-separation certificate.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The decisive separation theorem and detailed error derivations are imported, so the source alone does not reproduce the full proof chain.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From occupancy drift to a length-conditioned probabilistic model
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Exact block and interval censuses show height-dependent redistribution and apparent stabilization for adequately sampled lengths, motivating a block-length-conditioned distribution rather than a height-invariant Gram-law heuristic.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Long blocks remain too sparse, observed trends are finite-range, and no probabilistic mechanism is derived.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Exceptions as stress tests for both counting and search locality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Rosser-rule exceptions simultaneously test census conservation, require local recovery of displaced zero pairs, and reveal hypothetical patterns where an adjacent-block repair would be insufficient.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: All observed exceptions were locally repaired; the failure configuration is proposed but unobserved.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local amplitude, spacing, and exception geometry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Normalized close-pair spacing, local extrema of S(t), and large Gram-point values of Z(t) provide complementary scale-aware views of rare local zero configurations beyond categorical block types.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The examples and tail summaries are observational and plot extraction is incomplete, so they do not establish a universal relation among amplitude, spacing, and exception class.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite computation as a conditional analytic resource
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A rigorously certified finite critical-line range can strengthen the parameter in other conditional number-theoretic results while remaining logically distinct from a proof of the Riemann hypothesis.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The downstream results are only referenced, and their quantitative improvements are not worked out in this source.

within_source_saturation: All recoverable source-specific mechanisms are represented: finite certification, audit repair, numerical error control, exact occupancy/type statistics, rare-pattern search obstructions, local-extreme geometry, probabilistic modeling, and the finite/global scope boundary. Further segmentation would chiefly isolate individual table rows, repeat graph captions, or rely on defective plot/formula extraction.
